title: No cap
settingKo: 젊은 동료가 쓰는 슬랭 'no cap'을 배웁니다.

lines.text: That was the best pizza I've ever had, no cap.
lines.ko: 그거 내 인생 최고의 피자였어, 진짜로.

lines.text: Wait, what does 'no cap' mean? Like, no hat?
lines.ko: 잠깐, 'no cap'이 무슨 뜻이야? 모자 없다는 거야?

lines.text: Ha, no. 'Cap' means a lie, so 'no cap' means I'm being totally serious.
lines.ko: 하, 아니. 'cap'이 거짓말이라서 'no cap'은 완전 진심이라는 뜻이야.

lines.text: Got it. So if I exaggerate, you'd say 'that's cap'?
lines.ko: 알겠다. 그럼 내가 과장하면 '그거 cap이네'라고 하는 거지?

response.situationKo: 친구가 믿기 힘든 말을 합니다. 슬랭을 섞어 반응해 보세요.
response.prompt: I ran ten kilometers before breakfast this morning.

answers.text: That's cap. You can't even run for the bus.
No way. For real?
Seriously? That's impressive, if it's true.
Okay, no cap, I'm actually jealous.

title: It's giving
settingKo: 친구가 옷 스타일을 평가하며 'it's giving'을 씁니다.

lines.text: That jacket with those boots? It's giving nineties rock star.
lines.ko: 그 재킷에 그 부츠? 90년대 록스타 느낌이다.

lines.text: Is that a compliment? I can never tell with you.
lines.ko: 그거 칭찬이야? 너는 도통 모르겠어.

lines.text: It's a compliment! 'It's giving' just means it has that vibe.
lines.ko: 칭찬이야! 'It's giving'은 그 분위기가 난다는 뜻이야.

lines.text: Okay, then I'm keeping it. Main character energy all day.
lines.ko: 좋아, 그럼 이걸로 할래. 오늘 하루 주인공 느낌으로.

response.situationKo: 친구의 새 스타일이나 방을 슬랭으로 칭찬해 보세요.
response.prompt: What do you think of my new apartment?

answers.text: It's giving cozy café vibes. I'm obsessed.
Okay, the plants? Very main character energy.
I love it. It really suits you.
It's giving Paris apartment on a budget, in the best way.
answers.noteKo: in the best way로 칭찬임을 분명히 해요.

title: Lowkey, highkey
settingKo: 친구와 'lowkey', 'highkey'의 차이를 이야기합니다.

lines.text: I'm lowkey nervous about the interview tomorrow.
lines.ko: 내일 면접 은근히 긴장돼.

lines.text: Only lowkey? I'd be highkey panicking.
lines.ko: 은근히만? 나라면 대놓고 패닉일 거야.

lines.text: Ha. Lowkey means a little, or secretly. Highkey means very, and openly.
lines.ko: 하. lowkey는 조금이나 은근히, highkey는 아주, 대놓고라는 뜻이야.

lines.text: Well, I'm highkey sure you'll do great.
lines.ko: 음, 난 네가 잘할 거라고 대놓고 확신해.

response.situationKo: lowkey나 highkey를 써서 자신의 감정을 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: How do you feel about the trip next week?

answers.text: Highkey excited. I've been packing for a week.
Lowkey nervous about the flight, but mostly excited.
I'm really looking forward to it, honestly.
Lowkey can't wait. Highkey haven't booked a hotel.

title: Go touch grass
settingKo: 온라인 논쟁에 빠진 친구에게 'touch grass'라고 말합니다.

lines.text: I've been arguing with a stranger online about pineapple on pizza for three hours.
lines.ko: 모르는 사람이랑 피자에 파인애플 문제로 세 시간째 온라인에서 싸우는 중이야.

lines.text: Three hours? Bro, go touch grass.
lines.ko: 세 시간? 야, 밖에 좀 나가.

lines.text: Fair. I know it means I need to log off and see the real world.
lines.ko: 인정. 로그아웃하고 현실 세계 좀 보라는 뜻인 거 알아.

lines.text: Exactly. Come for a walk. The pizza debate will survive without you.
lines.ko: 바로 그거야. 산책 가자. 피자 논쟁은 너 없어도 살아남아.

response.situationKo: 게임이나 SNS에 너무 빠진 친구에게 장난스럽게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: I haven't left my room all weekend. New game came out.

answers.text: Okay, time to touch grass. Coffee in twenty minutes?
Log off and come get some fresh air with me.
Have you seen the sun this weekend? It misses you.
Maybe take a break and come for a walk later?

title: I got the ick
settingKo: 데이트 상대에게 갑자기 정이 떨어진 이야기를 합니다.

lines.text: Everything was perfect until he clapped when the plane landed. I got the ick.
lines.ko: 다 완벽했는데 비행기 착륙할 때 박수 치더라. 갑자기 정떨어졌어.

lines.text: The ick is so unfair. It's always something tiny.
lines.ko: 그 정떨어짐 진짜 불공평해. 항상 사소한 거잖아.

lines.text: I know. He's lovely, but now I can't unsee it.
lines.ko: 알아. 좋은 사람인데 이제 그게 계속 보여.

lines.text: Give it a week. Sometimes the ick wears off.
lines.ko: 일주일만 기다려 봐. 가끔 그 느낌이 사라지기도 해.

response.situationKo: 친구가 '정떨어진' 이유를 묻습니다. 사소한 이유를 재미있게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So why didn't the second date happen?

answers.text: Honestly? She chewed with her mouth open. Instant ick.
He called his mum 'mother'. I know, it's tiny, but I got the ick.
We just didn't click, I think.
He ran for a closing train door and missed. I couldn't recover.

title: He's got rizz
settingKo: 모임에서 인기 많은 친구를 'rizz'로 표현합니다.

lines.text: How did Jake get three phone numbers in one night?
lines.ko: 제이크는 어떻게 하룻밤에 번호를 세 개나 받았어?

lines.text: The man has rizz. He just talks to people like they're old friends.
lines.ko: 걔 매력이 있어. 사람들한테 오랜 친구처럼 말하잖아.

lines.text: Rizz comes from 'charisma', right?
lines.ko: rizz는 'charisma'에서 온 거지?

lines.text: Yep. And I have negative rizz, so I'm taking notes.
lines.ko: 응. 나는 마이너스 매력이라 메모하는 중이야.

response.situationKo: 친구의 사교성이나 매력을 슬랭으로 칭찬하거나 놀려 보세요.
response.prompt: Did you see how fast she made friends at the party?

answers.text: Unreal. She's got serious rizz.
She's a natural. I need her to teach me.
She has a lot of charisma. People just warm to her.
Meanwhile I spent twenty minutes talking to the dog.

title: It's a vibe
settingKo: 새로 생긴 바를 친구와 평가합니다.

lines.text: Candles, old records, tiny plates of food. This place is a vibe.
lines.ko: 촛불, 옛날 레코드, 작은 접시 음식. 여기 분위기 좋다.

lines.text: Agreed. Although the prices are also a vibe, and not a good one.
lines.ko: 동의. 근데 가격도 분위기 있다, 좋은 쪽은 아니고.

lines.text: Ha. One drink, then we go somewhere cheaper?
lines.ko: 하. 한 잔만 하고 더 싼 데 갈까?

lines.text: Deal. We'll call it a vibe check.
lines.ko: 좋아. 분위기 점검이라고 치자.

options: 한 잔만 하고 더 싼 곳으로 간다

response.situationKo: 처음 가 본 장소의 분위기를 캐주얼하게 평가해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, what do you think of this café?

answers.text: Total vibe. I could work here all day.
answers.noteKo: Total vibe는 완전 분위기 좋다는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Cozy vibes, but the music's a bit loud.
It's lovely. Very relaxing.
Honestly, not the vibe. Too many people on laptops.

title: Main character energy
settingKo: 혼자 여행 가는 친구를 응원합니다.

lines.text: I'm going to Lisbon alone next month. No plans, just vibes.
lines.ko: 다음 달에 혼자 리스본 가. 계획 없이 그냥 분위기 따라서.

lines.text: Love that. Very main character energy.
lines.ko: 좋다. 완전 주인공 같아.

lines.text: That's the plan: sit in cafés, write in a notebook, pretend I'm in a film.
lines.ko: 그게 계획이야. 카페에 앉아서 공책에 쓰고 영화 속에 있는 척하기.

lines.text: Just don't be the main character who misses her flight.
lines.ko: 비행기 놓치는 주인공만 되지 마.

response.situationKo: 친구의 대담한 계획을 슬랭으로 응원해 보세요.
response.prompt: I quit my job to learn to surf in Bali for six months.

answers.text: Iconic. Main character energy, honestly.
Love that for you. Send pictures.
answers.noteKo: Love that for you는 '너한테 너무 잘됐다'예요.

answers.text: Wow, that's brave. Go for it.
You're living the dream. I'm living the commute.

title: tbh, ngl, imo
settingKo: 외국인 친구의 문자 줄임말을 이해하지 못해 물어봅니다.

lines.text: My friend texted 'ngl the movie was mid tbh'. What does that even mean?
lines.ko: 친구가 'ngl the movie was mid tbh'라고 보냈어. 이게 무슨 뜻이야?

lines.text: 'Not gonna lie, the movie was average, to be honest.' Mid means mediocre.
lines.ko: '거짓말 안 하고, 영화 그저 그랬어, 솔직히.' mid는 평범하다는 뜻이야.

lines.text: And 'imo'? She uses it all the time.
lines.ko: 그럼 'imo'는? 걔 맨날 써.

lines.text: In my opinion. And 'fr' means for real. You'll pick them up fast.
lines.ko: 내 생각엔. 그리고 'fr'은 진짜로. 금방 익숙해질 거야.

response.situationKo: 친구에게 줄임말을 섞어 짧게 문자로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Text: did u like the new album??

answers.text: ngl it's fire. song 3 fr
tbh kinda mid imo
lowkey obsessed, been on repeat all day
Honestly, it's pretty good. The second half is better.

title: Why did you just say 'k'?
settingKo: 문자로 'k.' 한 글자만 받고 친구가 화났는지 걱정합니다.

lines.text: I told her I'd be late, and she replied 'k.' with a full stop. Is she angry?
lines.ko: 늦는다고 했더니 마침표 찍은 'k.'로 답했어. 화난 거야?

lines.text: A single 'k' with a full stop is definitely passive-aggressive.
lines.ko: 마침표 찍은 'k' 한 글자는 확실히 돌려서 화난 거야.

lines.text: Ugh. What if she'd sent 'okay!' instead?
lines.ko: 으. 대신 'okay!'라고 보냈다면?

lines.text: Then you'd be totally fine. Punctuation is basically tone of voice in texts.
lines.ko: 그럼 완전 괜찮은 거지. 문자에선 문장 부호가 사실상 목소리 톤이야.

phrases.en: Punctuation is tone of voice in texts.

response.situationKo: 약속에 늦는 친구에게 화나지 않았음을 문자로 확실히 보여 주세요.
response.prompt: Text: so sorry, running 20 min late!!

answers.text: No worries!! I'll grab us a table 😊
All good, take your time!
haha no stress, I'm still on the bus too
That's absolutely fine. See you soon.

title: What does that emoji mean?
settingKo: 같은 이모지도 세대마다 다르게 읽힌다는 걸 이야기합니다.

lines.text: My manager replied to my long email with just a thumbs-up. Is that rude?
lines.ko: 팀장님이 내 긴 메일에 엄지 이모지 하나로 답했어. 무례한 거야?

lines.text: To older people it just means 'got it'. To younger people it can feel cold.
lines.ko: 윗세대에겐 그냥 '알겠다'는 뜻이야. 젊은 세대에겐 차갑게 느껴질 수 있고.

lines.text: And the skull emoji? My little sister sends it after every joke.
lines.ko: 그럼 해골 이모지는? 여동생이 농담할 때마다 보내.

lines.text: That means 'I'm dead', as in laughing so hard. It's a compliment, weirdly.
lines.ko: '죽겠다', 너무 웃겨서 죽겠다는 뜻이야. 이상하게도 칭찬이야.

response.situationKo: 친구가 보낸 웃긴 영상에 슬랭으로 반응해 보세요.
response.prompt: Text: [sends a video of a cat falling off a sofa]

answers.text: I'm dead 💀💀
I can't 😭 the way it looked around after
Stop, I'm crying at work
Haha, that's hilarious. Poor cat.

title: Spill the tea
settingKo: 친구에게 회사 소문을 털어놓으라고 조릅니다.

lines.text: Okay, you've been smiling at your phone all day. Spill the tea.
lines.ko: 좋아, 하루 종일 폰 보면서 웃고 있잖아. 썰 풀어 봐.

lines.text: Fine. Remember the guy from the coffee shop? He finally asked me out.
lines.ko: 알았어. 카페 그 남자 기억나? 드디어 데이트 신청했어.

lines.text: No way! I need every detail. Start from the beginning.
lines.ko: 말도 안 돼! 하나도 빠짐없이 다 말해. 처음부터.

lines.text: There's not much tea yet. We're getting dinner on Friday.
lines.ko: 아직 썰이 많진 않아. 금요일에 저녁 먹기로 했어.

response.situationKo: 친구가 비밀이 있는 것 같아요. 털어놓으라고 장난스럽게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Nothing's going on, why do you ask?

answers.text: Come on, spill. I know that face.
Nothing? You've checked your phone ten times. Spill the tea.
Okay, but I want details later.
You seem really happy. Is there some good news?

title: Break a leg!
settingKo: 공연을 앞둔 친구에게 행운을 빕니다.

lines.text: My first stand-up comedy show is tonight. I'm terrified.
lines.ko: 오늘 밤 첫 스탠드업 코미디 공연이야. 너무 무서워.

lines.text: You'll be great. Break a leg!
lines.ko: 잘할 거야. 다리 부러지세요! (행운을 빌어!)

lines.text: I know it means good luck, but it still sounds threatening.
lines.ko: 행운을 빈다는 뜻인 건 아는데 그래도 협박처럼 들려.

lines.text: Actors think saying 'good luck' directly brings bad luck. Theater people are superstitious.
lines.ko: 배우들은 '행운을 빌어'라고 직접 말하면 불운이 온다고 생각해. 연극 하는 사람들은 미신을 믿거든.

options: '행운을 빌어'라고 직접 말하면 불운하다는 미신 때문

response.situationKo: 중요한 일을 앞둔 친구에게 자연스럽게 응원해 보세요.
response.prompt: My big presentation is in an hour.

answers.text: You've got this. Break a leg!
answers.noteKo: You've got this는 '넌 할 수 있어'예요.

answers.text: Go crush it! Text me after.
Knock 'em dead. You've practiced so much.
Good luck! I'm sure it'll go really well.

title: Bite the bullet
settingKo: 미루던 치과 예약을 하라고 친구가 떠밉니다.

lines.text: My tooth has been hurting for weeks, but I hate the dentist.
lines.ko: 몇 주째 이가 아픈데 치과가 너무 싫어.

lines.text: You've got to bite the bullet. It'll only get worse.
lines.ko: 이 악물고 가야 해. 더 나빠지기만 할 거야.

lines.text: I know, I know. I've been putting it off since March.
lines.ko: 알아, 알아. 3월부터 계속 미뤘어.

lines.text: Call them right now while I'm here. No excuses.
lines.ko: 나 있을 때 지금 당장 전화해. 핑계 없어.

options: 싫지만 피할 수 없는 일을 참고 하다

response.situationKo: 미뤄 온 일을 해야 하는 상황을 관용구로 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Have you told your landlord about the broken window yet?

answers.text: Not yet. I've been putting it off, but I'll bite the bullet today.
I'm dreading it, honestly. He's going to blame me.
No, but I'll call him this afternoon.
Okay, okay, biting the bullet right now. Wish me luck.

title: Feeling under the weather
settingKo: 몸이 안 좋다며 약속을 미룹니다.

lines.text: Still on for drinks tonight?
lines.ko: 오늘 밤 한잔 여전히 유효해?

lines.text: I'm feeling a bit under the weather, actually. Can we do next week?
lines.ko: 사실 몸이 좀 안 좋아. 다음 주에 할까?

lines.text: Of course. Rest up and drink lots of water.
lines.ko: 당연하지. 푹 쉬고 물 많이 마셔.

lines.text: Thanks. I'll be right as rain by Friday, I promise.
lines.ko: 고마워. 금요일엔 멀쩡해질 거야, 약속해.

phrases.en: I'm feeling a bit under the weather.

response.situationKo: 몸이 안 좋아 약속을 취소하는 메시지를 자연스럽게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Are you coming to the barbecue tomorrow?

answers.text: I'm a bit under the weather, so I'll have to take a rain check. Sorry!
Not feeling great, unfortunately. Save me a burger next time?
I'm sorry, I'm unwell and won't be able to make it.
Ugh, coming down with something. Have fun without me!
answers.noteKo: coming down with는 병이 오는 중이에요.

title: Not my cup of tea
settingKo: 친구가 추천한 공연이 취향이 아니라고 부드럽게 말합니다.

lines.text: So did you like the jazz concert I took you to?
lines.ko: 내가 데려간 재즈 공연 좋았어?

lines.text: Honestly, jazz isn't really my cup of tea, but the venue was beautiful.
lines.ko: 솔직히 재즈는 내 취향은 아닌데 공연장은 예뻤어.

lines.text: Fair enough. What is your cup of tea, then?
lines.ko: 그럴 수 있지. 그럼 네 취향은 뭐야?

lines.text: Loud rock shows where you can't hear yourself think.
lines.ko: 내 생각도 안 들릴 만큼 시끄러운 록 공연.

phrases.en: It's not really my cup of tea.

response.situationKo: 친구가 권한 것이 취향이 아니라고 기분 상하지 않게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Want to come to my yoga retreat this weekend?

answers.text: Thanks, but yoga's not really my cup of tea. Have an amazing time though!
It's not really my thing, but I'd be up for brunch after.
I appreciate the invite, but I'll pass this time.
Me, sitting still for two days? Not my cup of tea, sadly.

title: On the fence
settingKo: 새 휴대폰을 살지 고민하는 친구와 이야기합니다.

lines.text: Are you getting the new phone or not?
lines.ko: 새 폰 살 거야 말 거야?

lines.text: I'm still on the fence. Mine works fine, but the camera on the new one is amazing.
lines.ko: 아직 고민 중이야. 내 거 잘 되는데 새 거 카메라가 대박이야.

lines.text: Sleep on it. If you still want it next week, go for it.
lines.ko: 하룻밤 생각해 봐. 다음 주에도 갖고 싶으면 사.

lines.text: Good call. Impulse buys always come back to bite me.
lines.ko: 좋은 생각이야. 충동구매는 늘 나중에 후회하게 돼.

phrases.en: It'll come back to bite me.

response.situationKo: 아직 결정하지 못한 일에 대해 관용구로 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: So, are you moving to the new apartment?

answers.text: I'm still on the fence. It's bigger, but it's further from work.
Honestly, I'm torn. I'll sleep on it.
I haven't decided yet. I'm weighing the pros and cons.
Ask me tomorrow. Today's answer is maybe.

title: The ball's in your court
settingKo: 연락을 기다리는 친구에게 조언합니다.

lines.text: I sent him a long apology. Should I text again?
lines.ko: 그 사람한테 긴 사과 문자를 보냈어. 또 보낼까?

lines.text: No. You've done your part. The ball's in his court now.
lines.ko: 아니. 네 할 일은 했어. 이제 그 사람 차례야.

lines.text: Waiting is the worst part, though.
lines.ko: 그래도 기다리는 게 제일 힘들어.

lines.text: I know. Distract yourself. Let's go see a film.
lines.ko: 알아. 딴 데 정신 팔자. 영화 보러 가자.

response.situationKo: 협상이나 관계에서 이제 상대가 답할 차례라고 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Should I lower my price again for the client?

answers.text: No, you've made a fair offer. The ball's in their court now.
Don't. Let them come back to you first.
I'd wait. Lowering it twice makes you look desperate.
Hold your nerve. It's their move.
answers.noteKo: hold your nerve는 흔들리지 말라는 뜻이에요.

title: Time to hit the sack
settingKo: 밤늦게 영상 통화를 마무리합니다.

lines.text: Is it really one a.m.? I have to be up at six.
lines.ko: 진짜 새벽 1시야? 6시에 일어나야 하는데.

lines.text: Same. I'm going to hit the sack.
lines.ko: 나도. 이제 자러 갈래.

lines.text: Me too. I'm absolutely knackered.
lines.ko: 나도. 완전 녹초야.

lines.text: Night! Talk tomorrow, and don't scroll in bed.
lines.ko: 잘 자! 내일 얘기하고, 침대에서 폰 하지 마.

phrases.en: I'm going to hit the sack.

response.situationKo: 늦은 시간 대화를 자연스럽게 끝내는 말을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: One more episode?

answers.text: Nope, I'm calling it a night. I'm exhausted.
answers.noteKo: call it a night은 오늘은 여기까지라는 뜻이에요.

answers.text: Tempting, but I need to hit the sack.
I'm knackered. Same time tomorrow?
I'd better get some sleep. Good night!

title: Deadpan humor
settingKo: 무표정으로 농담하는 동료의 말을 진짜로 받아들여 당황합니다.

lines.text: The printer jammed again. I've decided to quit my job and become a farmer.
lines.ko: 프린터가 또 걸렸어. 회사 그만두고 농부가 되기로 했어.

lines.text: Wait, seriously? You're quitting?
lines.ko: 잠깐, 진짜? 그만둬?

lines.text: No. That's my deadpan face. You'll learn to read it.
lines.ko: 아니. 그게 내 무표정 농담 얼굴이야. 읽는 법을 배우게 될 거야.

lines.text: Great. Now I'll never know when you're being serious.
lines.ko: 좋네. 이제 네가 언제 진지한지 절대 모르겠다.

response.situationKo: 사소한 불편에 대해 무표정 과장 농담을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: The Wi-Fi's down again. How are you coping?

answers.text: Barely. I've started talking to my plants for company.
I've decided to live in the woods. Please forward my mail.
As you can see, I'm handling it with great dignity.
Annoying, but I'm getting other work done.

title: Making fun of yourself
settingKo: 실수를 자기 농담으로 넘기는 법을 배웁니다.

lines.text: Did you really send the birthday email to the whole company instead of just Tom?
lines.ko: 진짜 생일 메일을 톰한테만이 아니라 전사에 보냈어?

lines.text: I did. Two hundred people now know Tom loves cats. My talent for disaster is unmatched.
lines.ko: 응. 이제 200명이 톰이 고양이 좋아하는 걸 알아. 사고 치는 재능은 내가 따라올 사람이 없지.

lines.text: Ha! At least you can laugh about it.
lines.ko: 하! 그래도 웃어넘길 수 있네.

lines.text: If I don't laugh, I'll have to hide under my desk until Christmas.
lines.ko: 안 웃으면 크리스마스까지 책상 밑에 숨어 있어야 할 거야.

gist.questionKo: 두 번째 사람이 실수에 대처한 방식은?

phrases.en: My talent for disaster is unmatched.
phrases.ko: 사고 치는 재능은 따라올 사람이 없지.

phrases.en: At least you can laugh about it.

response.situationKo: 자신의 작은 실수를 자기 농담으로 가볍게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why are you wearing two different shoes?

answers.text: It's a new trend. I'm starting it, clearly.
My talent for getting dressed in the dark strikes again.
Completely on purpose. Very fashion-forward.
Oh no, I didn't even notice. Long morning!

title: Dad jokes
settingKo: 아빠의 아재 개그에 반응하는 법을 배웁니다.

lines.text: Did you hear about the restaurant on the moon? Great food, no atmosphere.
lines.ko: 달에 있는 식당 얘기 들었어? 음식은 좋은데 분위기(대기)가 없대.

lines.text: Dad, that's terrible.
lines.ko: 아빠, 그거 최악이야.

lines.text: Then why are you smiling?
lines.ko: 그럼 왜 웃고 있니?

lines.text: Because it's so bad it's actually good. That's the whole point of a dad joke.
lines.ko: 너무 별로라서 오히려 좋아서. 그게 아재 개그의 핵심이잖아.

phrases.en: It's so bad it's actually good.

response.situationKo: 누군가 아재 개그를 했어요. 신음하면서도 즐겁게 반응해 보세요.
response.prompt: Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts.

answers.text: Groan. That's so bad it's good.
I hate that I laughed at that.
Stop. Please. Okay, tell me another one.
Ha, that's a classic.

title: Yeah, no
settingKo: 원어민이 쓰는 'yeah, no'와 'no, yeah'의 차이를 배웁니다.

lines.text: I asked my Aussie coworker if she wanted to work on Saturday, and she said 'yeah, no'.
lines.ko: 호주 동료한테 토요일에 일할 거냐고 물었더니 'yeah, no'라고 했어.

lines.text: That's a no. The 'yeah' just means 'I hear you'.
lines.ko: 그건 '아니'야. 'yeah'는 그냥 '네 말 들었어'라는 뜻이고.

lines.text: So 'no, yeah' means yes?
lines.ko: 그럼 'no, yeah'는 '응'이야?

lines.text: Usually, yes. The last word is the real answer.
lines.ko: 보통은 그래. 마지막 단어가 진짜 대답이야.

phrases.en: The last word is the real answer.

response.situationKo: 'yeah, no'나 'no, yeah'로 자연스럽게 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Do you fancy a run in the rain?

answers.text: Yeah, no. Hard pass.
No, yeah, actually, count me in.
Yeah, no, I'll be on the sofa, thanks.
I think I'll skip it this time.

title: Was that sarcastic?
settingKo: 친구의 말이 진심인지 빈정거림인지 헷갈립니다.

lines.text: Oh, great, another team meeting. I just love meetings.
lines.ko: 오, 좋다, 또 팀 회의네. 나 회의 정말 좋아해.

lines.text: Really? I didn't know you enjoyed them.
lines.ko: 정말? 회의 좋아하는 줄 몰랐어.

lines.text: I was being sarcastic. Listen to the flat tone and the 'just'.
lines.ko: 빈정거린 거야. 밋밋한 톤이랑 'just'를 잘 들어 봐.

lines.text: Ah, the words say love, but the voice says please help me.
lines.ko: 아, 말은 좋다는데 목소리는 살려 달라는 거구나.

phrases.en: The words say love, but the voice says...

response.situationKo: 귀찮은 상황에 대해 빈정거리는 말을 해 보세요.
response.prompt: The train's delayed by an hour.

answers.text: Oh, perfect. Just what I needed today.
Wonderful. I love standing on cold platforms.
Love that for me.
That's annoying. I'll grab a coffee while we wait.

title: No worries, mate
settingKo: 호주 친구의 표현을 하나씩 배웁니다.

lines.text: Wanna grab a coffee this arvo? I'll shout.
lines.ko: 오늘 오후에 커피 한잔할래? 내가 쏠게.

lines.text: Arvo means afternoon, right? And 'I'll shout' means you'll pay?
lines.ko: arvo는 오후 맞지? 그리고 'I'll shout'은 네가 산다는 거지?

lines.text: Spot on. You're picking up Aussie slang heaps fast.
lines.ko: 정확해. 호주 슬랭 엄청 빨리 배운다.

lines.text: Cheers, mate. See you at three, then. No worries.
lines.ko: 고마워, 친구. 그럼 3시에 봐. 걱정 마.

response.situationKo: 호주식 표현을 섞어 친구의 제안에 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: Barbie at mine this arvo?

answers.text: Sounds heaps good, mate. I'll bring the drinks.
Reckon I can make it by four. Cheers!
No worries. Need me to bring anything?
Sounds great! What time should I come?

title: Gutted and knackered
settingKo: 영국 친구가 쓰는 감정 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: We lost the final in the last minute. I'm absolutely gutted.
lines.ko: 결승에서 마지막 1분에 졌어. 완전 속상해.

lines.text: Gutted means really disappointed, right?
lines.ko: gutted는 정말 실망했다는 뜻이지?

lines.text: Yeah. And after running for ninety minutes, I'm knackered too.
lines.ko: 응. 그리고 90분을 뛰었더니 녹초이기도 해.

lines.text: Fancy a cuppa? That's the British cure for everything, isn't it?
lines.ko: 차 한잔할래? 그게 영국식 만병통치약 아니야?

response.situationKo: 영국식 표현을 섞어 하루를 묘사해 보세요.
response.prompt: How was your day?

answers.text: Absolutely knackered. Fancy a cuppa?
Brilliant, actually. Got the job!
Bit rubbish, to be honest. Train was cancelled again.
Gutted. My team lost. Cheers for asking, though.

title: Y'all and fixin' to
settingKo: 텍사스 출신 동료의 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: Y'all want some sweet tea? I'm fixin' to make a fresh pitcher.
lines.ko: 다들 스위트티 마실래? 이제 막 새로 한 주전자 만들려던 참이야.

lines.text: 'Fixin' to' means 'about to', right?
lines.ko: 'fixin' to'는 '막 ~하려던 참'이라는 뜻이지?

lines.text: Sure does. And 'y'all' is just 'you all'. Saves time.
lines.ko: 맞아. 그리고 'y'all'은 'you all'이야. 시간 절약이지.

lines.text: Honestly, it's more useful than 'you guys'. I'm stealing it.
lines.ko: 솔직히 'you guys'보다 유용하다. 훔쳐 갈게.

phrases.en: I'm fixin' to make some tea.

response.situationKo: 남부식 표현을 섞어 여러 사람에게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: We're heading out to eat. Coming?

answers.text: Y'all go ahead. I'm fixin' to finish this email.
Sure thing. Y'all save me a seat.
Reckon I'll be right there in five.
Yes, give me five minutes!

title: What's the craic?
settingKo: 아일랜드 친구의 인사 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: Ah, there you are! What's the craic?
lines.ko: 아, 왔구나! 별일 없어?

lines.text: The crack? Is that something illegal?
lines.ko: 크랙? 그거 불법적인 거야?

lines.text: Ha! No, craic means fun or news. 'What's the craic' just means 'what's up'.
lines.ko: 하! 아니, craic은 재미나 소식이야. 'What's the craic'은 그냥 '잘 지내?'라는 뜻이야.

lines.text: Phew. Grand, then. The craic is that I finally found a flat.
lines.ko: 휴. 그럼 좋아. 소식은 드디어 집을 구했다는 거야.

response.situationKo: 'What's the craic?'에 자연스럽게 근황으로 답해 보세요.
response.prompt: What's the craic?

answers.text: Grand, thanks. Not much craic here. Yourself?
The craic is I'm finally on holiday!
All good. Same old, same old.
Not bad at all! How are you?

title: Toques and double-doubles
settingKo: 캐나다 친구의 겨울 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: It's minus twenty out there, eh? Don't forget your toque.
lines.ko: 밖에 영하 20도야, 그치? 털모자 잊지 마.

lines.text: A toque is a winter hat, right? And why do you say 'eh' so much?
lines.ko: toque가 겨울 모자 맞지? 그리고 왜 'eh'를 그렇게 자주 해?

lines.text: It just turns things into a friendly question, like 'right?' Want a double-double on the way?
lines.ko: 그냥 '그렇지?'처럼 친근한 질문으로 만드는 거야. 가는 길에 더블더블 마실래?

lines.text: Let me guess: two sugars and two creams?
lines.ko: 맞혀 볼게. 설탕 둘에 크림 둘?

response.situationKo: 캐나다식 'eh'를 넣어 날씨 이야기를 해 보세요.
response.prompt: Cold enough for you?

answers.text: Brutal, eh? Good thing I brought my toque.
Tell me about it. My coffee froze on the way here.
Freezing, eh? Let's get inside.
It's very cold today, isn't it?

title: Standing on line
settingKo: 뉴요커 친구의 빠른 말투와 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: We stood on line for an hour for that bagel, and honestly? Worth it.
lines.ko: 그 베이글 사려고 한 시간 줄 섰는데, 솔직히? 그럴 만했어.

lines.text: On line? I thought it was 'in line'.
lines.ko: on line? 'in line' 아니야?

lines.text: Most of the country says 'in line', but plenty of New Yorkers say 'on line'.
lines.ko: 대부분은 'in line'이라고 하는데 뉴요커들은 'on line'이라고 많이 해.

lines.text: Noted. Next time I'll stand on line like a local.
lines.ko: 기억할게. 다음엔 현지인처럼 줄 서 볼게.

gist.questionKo: 뉴욕 사람들이 'in line' 대신 쓰는 표현은?

phrases.en: We stood on line for an hour.

response.situationKo: 줄을 오래 선 경험을 빠르고 캐주얼하게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: How long did you wait for those concert tickets?

answers.text: Stood on line for three hours. Honestly? Totally worth it.
Forever. Like, I aged a year in that queue.
About two hours in line, but we got front row.
Way too long. Never again. Probably.

title: Gonna, wanna, gotta
settingKo: 원어민이 빨리 말할 때 줄어드는 소리를 배웁니다.

lines.text: I'm gonna grab lunch. Wanna come, or you gotta work?
lines.ko: 나 점심 먹으러 갈 건데. 같이 갈래, 아님 일해야 돼?

lines.text: I gotta finish this first, but I'm gonna be quick.
lines.ko: 이거 먼저 끝내야 하는데 금방 할게.

lines.text: Cool. You know these are just 'going to', 'want to', and 'got to', said fast?
lines.ko: 좋아. 이게 그냥 'going to', 'want to', 'got to'를 빨리 말한 거라는 거 알지?

lines.text: I do now. I just wouldn't write them in a work email.
lines.ko: 이제 알아. 업무 메일에는 안 쓸 거지만.

gist.questionKo: 'gonna, wanna, gotta'는 어디에 쓰면 안 되나요?

response.situationKo: gonna, wanna, gotta를 써서 주말 계획을 빠르게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: What are you doing this weekend?

answers.text: I'm gonna sleep in, then I gotta clean my flat.
Wanna go hiking? I'm gonna be free on Sunday.
Gotta work Saturday, but Sunday I'm gonna do nothing.
I'm going to visit my parents, probably.

title: Whaddya mean?
settingKo: 'What do you'가 'whaddya'로 들리는 현상을 배웁니다.

lines.text: Whaddya wanna do tonight? Didja see the new place on Main Street?
lines.ko: 오늘 밤 뭐 할래? 메인 스트리트에 새로 생긴 데 봤어?

lines.text: Sorry, 'whaddya' and 'didja'? Can you say that slower?
lines.ko: 미안, 'whaddya'랑 'didja'? 천천히 말해 줄래?

lines.text: 'What do you want to do' and 'Did you see'. We blur the words together when we talk fast.
lines.ko: 'What do you want to do'랑 'Did you see'. 빨리 말할 때 단어를 뭉개.

lines.text: That explains why I understand films with subtitles but not real conversations.
lines.ko: 그래서 자막 있는 영화는 알아듣는데 실제 대화는 못 알아듣는구나.

phrases.ko: 뭐 할래? (What do you want to do)

response.situationKo: 빠른 말을 못 알아들었을 때 자연스럽게 다시 부탁해 보세요.
response.prompt: Whaddya think, d'ya wanna split a cab or what?

answers.text: Sorry, come again? Did you say split a cab?
One more time, a bit slower? My ears are tired.
Oh, share a taxi? Yeah, sounds good.
I'm sorry, could you repeat that?

title: Like, you know
settingKo: 원어민이 생각할 시간을 벌 때 쓰는 군말을 배웁니다.

lines.text: So the meeting was, like, super long, and, you know, nobody actually decided anything.
lines.ko: 그래서 회의가, 뭐랄까, 엄청 길었고, 있잖아, 아무도 실제로 결정을 안 했어.

lines.text: You say 'like' and 'you know' a lot. Does it mean something?
lines.ko: 'like'랑 'you know'를 많이 쓰네. 무슨 뜻이 있어?

lines.text: Not really. It just fills the gap while I think, like 'um' does.
lines.ko: 별로. 'um'처럼 생각하는 동안 빈틈을 메우는 거야.

lines.text: Good to know. Using a few makes me sound natural, but too many sounds nervous.
lines.ko: 알아 두면 좋겠다. 조금 쓰면 자연스럽고, 너무 많이 쓰면 긴장해 보이겠네.

response.situationKo: 군말을 적당히 섞어 최근 있었던 일을 자연스럽게 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: How was the party last night?

answers.text: It was, like, really fun, but, you know, kind of loud.
Honestly? Basically just a lot of people talking about work.
So, um, I didn't know anyone, but it was kind of nice.
It was very enjoyable. I met some interesting people.

title: Kinda, sorta, ish
settingKo: 확신이 없을 때 쓰는 애매한 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: What time are you coming? Seven?
lines.ko: 몇 시에 와? 7시?

lines.text: Seven-ish. I'm kinda stuck at work, so sorta depends.
lines.ko: 7시쯤? 일에 좀 묶여 있어서 좀 상황 봐야 돼.

lines.text: 'Ish' means roughly, right? So seven fifteen is fine?
lines.ko: 'ish'는 대략이라는 거지? 그럼 7시 15분도 괜찮은 거지?

lines.text: Exactly. And if I say 'seven-ish-ish', expect eight.
lines.ko: 바로 그거야. 그리고 내가 '7시쯤쯤'이라고 하면 8시로 생각해.

response.situationKo: 확실하지 않은 계획을 '-ish', 'kinda'를 써서 말해 보세요.
response.prompt: Are you hungry?

answers.text: Kinda. Snack-ish hungry, not dinner hungry.
Sorta? I could eat, I guess.
A bit. Maybe in an hour-ish?
Yes, a little. Shall we get something?

title: How are you? Fine!
settingKo: 'How are you?'가 진짜 질문이 아닌 인사라는 걸 배웁니다.

lines.text: The cashier asked how I was, so I told her about my back pain and my landlord.
lines.ko: 계산원이 어떻게 지내냐고 해서 허리 통증이랑 집주인 얘기를 했어.

lines.text: Ha! In a shop, 'How are you?' is basically just 'hello'.
lines.ko: 하! 가게에서 'How are you?'는 사실상 그냥 '안녕'이야.

lines.text: So what am I supposed to say?
lines.ko: 그럼 뭐라고 해야 해?

lines.text: 'Good, thanks, you?' Save the real answer for friends who actually ask twice.
lines.ko: '좋아요, 고마워요, 당신은요?' 진짜 대답은 두 번 물어보는 친구를 위해 아껴 둬.

response.situationKo: 상황에 맞게 'How are you?'에 답해 보세요. (가게 직원)
response.prompt: Hi there, how are you today?

answers.text: Good, thanks! You?
Not bad, thanks. How's your day going?
Great, thank you. And you?
Surviving! You?

title: We should hang out sometime
settingKo: '언젠가 만나자'가 진짜 약속인지 헷갈립니다.

lines.text: She said 'we should totally hang out sometime', but she never followed up.
lines.ko: 걔가 '언젠가 꼭 만나자'고 했는데 연락이 없어.

lines.text: 'Sometime' is often just polite. It's not a real plan until there's a day and time.
lines.ko: '언젠가'는 보통 그냥 예의상 하는 말이야. 날짜랑 시간이 있어야 진짜 계획이지.

lines.text: So how do I tell if she means it?
lines.ko: 그럼 진심인지 어떻게 알아?

lines.text: Suggest something specific, like coffee on Thursday. If she says yes, she meant it.
lines.ko: 목요일에 커피처럼 구체적으로 제안해 봐. 좋다고 하면 진심이었던 거야.

response.situationKo: 누군가 '언젠가 보자'고 할 때, 진짜 약속으로 만들어 보세요.
response.prompt: We should grab a drink sometime!

answers.text: Definitely! Are you free Thursday after work?
Let's actually do it. How about Saturday?
I'd like that. I'll message you this week.
Yes! Before we both get busy and forget, what's your number?

title: I'll think about it
settingKo: '생각해 볼게요'가 사실상 거절인 경우를 배웁니다.

lines.text: I pitched my idea to the client, and they said, 'Interesting, we'll think about it.'
lines.ko: 고객에게 아이디어를 제안했더니 '흥미롭네요, 생각해 볼게요'라고 했어.

lines.text: Hmm. Did they ask any follow-up questions or mention next steps?
lines.ko: 흠. 후속 질문을 하거나 다음 단계를 말했어?

lines.text: No, they just thanked me and ended the call.
lines.ko: 아니, 그냥 고맙다고 하고 통화를 끝냈어.

lines.text: Then it's probably a polite no. A real 'maybe' usually comes with questions.
lines.ko: 그럼 아마 정중한 거절일 거야. 진짜 '아마도'는 보통 질문이 따라와.

response.situationKo: 상대의 애매한 답이 진짜인지 정중하게 확인해 보세요.
response.prompt: We'll think about it and get back to you.

answers.text: Of course. Is there anything holding you back that I could address now?
Thanks. When would be a good time to follow up?
Would it help if I sent a shorter summary with prices?
Totally fair. Honestly, if it's a no, that's fine too. Just let me know.

title: I'm good
settingKo: 'I'm good'이 '괜찮다(사양)'로 쓰이는 걸 배웁니다.

lines.text: Can I get you another drink?
lines.ko: 음료 한 잔 더 드릴까요?

lines.text: I'm good, thanks.
lines.ko: 괜찮아요, 고마워요.

lines.text: Wait, does 'I'm good' mean yes, you're happy, or no, you don't want one?
lines.ko: 잠깐, 'I'm good'은 네 좋다는 거야, 아니면 필요 없다는 거야?

lines.text: In this case, no thanks. It means I already have what I need.
lines.ko: 이 경우엔 사양이야. 이미 필요한 게 있다는 뜻이야.

phrases.en: I already have what I need.

response.situationKo: 권유를 'I'm good' 같은 표현으로 자연스럽게 사양해 보세요.
response.prompt: Want some of my fries?

answers.text: I'm good, thanks!
I'm all set, but thanks for offering.
Tempting, but I'm full. Maybe later.
No, thank you. I've just eaten.

title: My bad!
settingKo: 작은 실수에 쓰는 가벼운 사과 표현을 배웁니다.

lines.text: Hey, you took my coffee. That one's the oat latte.
lines.ko: 야, 내 커피 가져갔어. 그건 오트 라떼야.

lines.text: Oh, my bad! Here you go.
lines.ko: 아, 내 실수! 여기.

lines.text: No worries. They look exactly the same.
lines.ko: 괜찮아. 완전 똑같이 생겼잖아.

lines.text: Still, I owe you one. Next round's on me.
lines.ko: 그래도 신세 졌다. 다음 건 내가 살게.

response.situationKo: 작은 실수를 했을 때 가볍게 사과하고 만회해 보세요.
response.prompt: You forgot to save me a seat!

answers.text: My bad! I'll grab you a chair.
Oh no, totally forgot. I owe you one.
answers.noteKo: I owe you one으로 만회를 약속해요.

answers.text: Sorry! Take mine, I'll stand.
I'm so sorry, that was careless of me.

title: Dodging a nosy question
settingKo: 사적인 질문을 웃으며 피하는 법을 배웁니다.

lines.text: So how much do you earn at your new job? Must be a lot!
lines.ko: 그래서 새 직장에서 얼마 벌어? 많이 벌겠지!

lines.text: Ha, enough to buy my own coffee, at least. How's your kitchen renovation going?
lines.ko: 하, 적어도 내 커피 사 먹을 만큼은. 너네 부엌 공사는 어떻게 돼 가?

lines.text: Oh, it's a nightmare. The tiles came in the wrong color.
lines.ko: 아, 악몽이야. 타일이 색이 잘못 왔어.

lines.text: No way. Tell me everything.
lines.ko: 말도 안 돼. 다 얘기해 봐.

gist.questionKo: 두 번째 사람이 질문을 피한 방법은?
options: 농담 후 화제를 상대 이야기로 돌렸다

phrases.en: Enough to buy my own coffee.
phrases.ko: 적어도 내 커피 사 먹을 만큼. (얼버무리기)

response.situationKo: 사적인 질문을 웃으며 피하고 화제를 바꿔 보세요.
response.prompt: So when are you two getting married?

answers.text: Ha, you'll be the first to know. Anyway, how was your holiday?
Who knows! We're just enjoying things as they are. How about you?
No plans yet. Did you end up getting that new job, by the way?
I'd rather not talk about that tonight, if that's okay.
